title: Scheduled supply-chain audit
summary: Dependency and extension audits run on a schedule and after every install or update, with findings dispositioned.

protected.asset: Installed code, extensions and images the deployment runs
protected.failure: A vulnerable or malicious dependency or extension remains deployed because nobody looked after an update.

rationale: Extensions, images and lazy installs change the executed code base without a human review step. A scheduled audit plus an after-change audit, with each finding explicitly dispositioned, closes the gap between 'installed' and 'known'. Findings that are accepted get an expiry, not a silent pass.

variants.description: Use the deployment's own security audit command in a scheduled job with a fail-on threshold the owner chose.
Native audit plus a pinned-image SBOM review and scheduled rescans with expiring ignores.

verification.method: Read the scheduled audit job, its threshold, its delivery target and the last run's outcome; confirm the most recent install or update event has a corresponding audit run.
verification.evidence: Job definition summary, last-run outcome and disposition list; no environment contents.

rollback.method: Pause or remove the audit job; record who accepted the reduced visibility.

failure_modes: The audit runs but findings are never dispositioned, drifting into noise.
The job's delivery target is broken, so failures reach nobody.
Lazy installs occur between scheduled runs and are never audited.
